newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sells 45.9 billion bolivars of TEM bills. [CORRECTED 18:12 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sells 45.9 billion bolivars of TEM bills. [CORRECTED 18:12 GMT]

text.p: Venezuela's Central Bank said it sold 30 billion bolivars of 180-day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills at a price of 98.78 (corrects from 99.78) percent.
The 180-day bills carried a 27.93 percent coupon.

The bank also sold 5.906 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 28.87 percent coupon at a price of 96.18 percent, and 10 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 29.86 percent coupon at an average price of 94.26 percent.
The bank had offered 30 billion bolivars of 180-day notes, 10 billion of 269-day notes, and 10 billion of 358-day notes.

According to a preliminary calculation by Reuters using the Central Bank's method, the yield on the notes was 28.43 percent for the 180-day TEMs, 35.33 percent on the 269-day notes, and 37.79 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
At last week's auction, the bank sold 180-, 269- and 358-day bills with yields of 30.75 (corrects from 27.93), 32.27 and 34.85 percent respectively.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
